rules.rule: Extract 'right' only when it is part of a anatomical location description involving brain regions (e.g., 'right inferior parietal', 'right temporal', 'right occipital lobe') or cardiac structures (e.g., 'right ventricular', 'right atrial') with clinical imaging or neurological findings.

Skip 'right' when it appears in the context of imaging modalities (e.g., 'CXR', 'EKG') or as part of a section header (e.g., 'EKG (___):') or lab result context (e.g., 'Right bundle branch block') without anatomical specificity.

Extract 'right' only if it is immediately followed by a anatomical structure (e.g., 'right hilum', 'right ventricular free wall', 'right inferior parietal') and appears in a clinical narrative describing findings (e.g., infarct, abnormality, motion).

Extract 'L' only when it appears as a standalone anatomical laterality marker immediately before a body part or region (e.g., 'L flank pain', 'L side', 'L oophorectomy'), and the context indicates clinical assessment or history of a condition.

Skip 'L' when it appears in motor/sensory exam tables (e.g., 'Delt Bic Tri WrE FFl FE IO IP Quad Ham TA ___') or reflex tables (e.g., 'Bi Tri ___ Pat Ach') where it is part of a structured assessment header or row label.
Skip 'L' when it is part of a section header or label such as 'L Normal (x) Abnormal ()' or 'L ___ years ago' if the text is in a list format with no clinical descriptor of a condition or body part.

Extract 'R' only when it appears as a standalone laterality marker immediately before a body part or region in a structured exam section (e.g., 'R Normal (x) Abnormal ()', 'R distal dorsal arm', 'R foot more edematous'), and only if it is not part of a table header or row with other anatomical terms.

Skip 'R' when it appears in a table header or row that includes other anatomical terms or markers (e.g., 'Bi Tri Pat Ach', 'Delt Bic Tri WrE FFl FE IO IP Quad Ham TA ___'), even if it is followed by a body part.

Skip 'R' when it appears in a section labeled with 'R Normal (x) Abnormal ()' or similar structured format, unless it is immediately followed by a body part or region in a non-table context (e.g., 'R foot more edematous').

Extract 'left' only when it appears as a standalone anatomical laterality marker immediately before a body part or region in a structured list or clinical description (e.g., 'left piriformis syndrome', 'left eye opens', 'left centrum semiovale').

Skip 'left' when it appears in a non-anatomical context such as 'left humerus' in a procedural or follow-up note, or when it is part of a phrase indicating time or sequence (e.g., 'left shift', 'left ___ days', 'left ___ years ago').
Skip 'left' when it appears in a section header or label such as 'Left ___' or 'Left Normal (x) Abnormal ()', unless it is directly followed by a body part or region in a clinical description.

Extract 'pain' only when it appears in a clinical context describing a symptom, such as in History of Present Illness, physical exam, or chief complaint sections, and is followed by descriptors like 'sharp', 'pleuritic', 'worse with', or 'localized to'.

Skip 'pain' when it appears in a sentence describing pain control or resolution, such as 'pain was well-controlled' or 'pain resolved', especially in sections like Hospital Course or Review of Systems.
Skip 'pain' when it appears in a negated or conditional context, such as 'no pain', 'pain not present', or 'pain was not felt to be due to', particularly in diagnostic or assessment statements.

Extract 'normal' only when it is part of a clinical assessment of anatomical structure or function (e.g., 'ventricular function is normal', 'wall motion is normal'), and is immediately followed by a structural or functional descriptor (e.g., 'motion', 'size', 'function', 'effusion') or appears in a structured report section like TTE, ECHO, CXR, or Physical Exam.

Skip 'normal' when it appears in a section header, conclusion, or impression line (e.g., 'IMPRESSION: Normal global and regional biventricular'), or when it is part of a laboratory result format (e.g., 'HYPOCHROM-NORMAL', 'ANISOCYT-1+'), or when it is used in a non-clinical descriptive context such as 'normal appearance' without functional or structural detail.

Skip 'normal' when it is part of a lab value format with hyphenated terms (e.g., 'ANISOCYT-1+', 'MACROCYT-1+', 'POLYCHROM-NORMAL'), or when it follows a label like '___' in a result line (e.g., '___ 09:50PM   HYPOCHROM-NORMAL'), indicating a result field rather than a clinical assessment.

Extract 'wbc' only when it appears in a lab value line formatted as 'WBC-<value>' or 'WBC: <value>' with a numeric value immediately following, and the line contains other lab markers like 'RBC', 'Hgb', 'Hct', or 'Plt'.

Skip 'wbc' when it appears in free-text narrative within History of Present Illness or similar sections, especially when followed by 'normal', 'elevated', or 'left shift' without a numeric value or lab format.

Skip 'wbc' when it appears as part of a phrase like 'WBC 13.1' or 'WBC 13' without a hyphen or colon delimiter, and not within a structured lab line containing multiple lab values (e.g., 'RBC: 4.24', 'Hgb: 11.7').

Extract 'ct' only when it appears as part of a structured imaging modality name with a body region, such as 'CT torso', 'CT-torso', 'CT of your head', or 'CT on ___ showed', and is followed by a clinical finding or diagnostic purpose.

Skip 'ct' when it appears in a free-text narrative within section headers like 'Admission Labs', 'Discharge Labs', or 'CONTRAINDICATIONS FOR IV CONTRAST', especially when followed by 'with contrast' or 'prior to admission' without a clinical finding.

Skip 'ct' when it appears in a sentence that only references prior imaging without a new clinical indication, such as 'CT from ___ suggesting this' or 'CT with contrast is not able to provide', especially if the chunk contains no new diagnostic or therapeutic purpose.

Extract 'glucose' only when it appears in a lab value line with a numeric value following a hyphen or colon delimiter (e.g., 'Glucose-158*', 'Glucose: 82'), and the chunk contains other lab values in the same format.
Skip 'glucose' when it appears in free-text narrative such as 'morning glucose 140s-150s' or 'blood sugars improved', even if preceded by a time stamp or section header.

Skip 'glucose' when the chunk contains only non-numeric text around it, such as 'Glucose: 82' with no surrounding lab values or structured format, especially if it appears in a section labeled 'LABORATORY DATA' or similar.

Extract 'pulmonary' only when it appears as a section header followed by a colon and clinical assessment (e.g., 'Pulmonary: The patient remained stable...'), or when part of a pathological diagnosis describing origin (e.g., 'carcinoma of pulmonary origin').

Skip 'pulmonary' when it appears in a phrase like 'from a pulmonary standpoint' or 'pulmonary toilet' unless immediately followed by a clinical assessment or diagnostic term (e.g., 'pulmonary toilet, early ambulation' is not a valid extraction).

Skip 'pulmonary' when it appears in a sentence that only describes monitoring or stability without clinical evaluation (e.g., 'The patient remained stable from a pulmonary standpoint'), unless the sentence includes a diagnostic or functional assessment.

Extract 'cta' only when it appears as part of a structured imaging modality name with a body region, such as 'CTA of the chest' or 'CTA head and neck', and is followed by clinical findings or imaging interpretation.

Skip 'cta' when it appears in a free-text narrative without a clinical indication, especially when followed by 'was deferred', 'was unable to undergo', or 'was not performed', indicating non-execution or exclusion.

Skip 'cta' when it appears in a section header or label such as 'CTA HEAD AND NECK ___ (PRELIM)' or 'CTA: No definite vascular abnormalities', unless immediately followed by clinical findings or interpretation of results.

Extract 'stroke' only when it appears in a structured clinical context such as section headers (e.g., 'Discharge Diagnosis: TIA or Stroke'), within a sentence describing a clinical event (e.g., 'new infarct involving the right inferior' or 'workup for stroke'), or in a clinical scale (e.g., 'NIHSS performed... Stroke Scale Score: 9').

Skip 'stroke' when it appears in a free-text narrative within a section header or label such as 'Stroke Service' or 'admitted to the stroke service' unless immediately followed by a clinical finding or assessment (e.g., 'admitted to the stroke service. Upon admission, underlying cause was evaluated').

Extract 'stroke' only when it is part of a clinical diagnosis or assessment phrase such as 'prior stroke with residual hemiparesis' or 'new stroke that was thought to be secondary to another medical cause', but skip when it appears in a phrase like 'right sided heaviness' or 'baseline deficit' without explicit reference to a clinical stroke event.
Extract 'urine' only when it appears as part of a structured lab line with a time stamp and at least one lab parameter (e.g., '___ 10:00PM URINE RBC-4*', '___ 02:46PM URINE WBC-1').
Skip 'urine' when it appears in a free-text line without a time stamp and lab parameters, such as 'URINE Color-Straw' or 'Blood-NEG Nitrite-NEG', especially when not preceded by a time-stamped line.
Skip 'urine' when it appears in section headers or labels like 'URINE CULTURE (Final ___:' or 'MICROBIOLOGY:' unless followed by a time-stamped lab line with parameters.

Extract 'negative' only when it appears in a clinical test or imaging result context with a clear modality or test name preceding it, such as 'U/S negative for DVT' or 'troponins negative', and when followed by a clinical conclusion or assessment.
Skip 'negative' when it appears in a free-text narrative or section header without a specific test or modality reference, such as 'negative in ED' or 'negative for DVT' without a preceding test name.

Skip 'negative' when it appears in a line that is part of a labeled test report section (e.g., 'GMS stain for fungal organisms is negative') unless the test name is explicitly linked to a clinical finding or diagnosis.
Extract 'ra' only when it appears as part of a structured oxygen saturation or oxygen therapy notation with a value and unit, such as 'SaO2: 100% RA' or '98% RA' or 'On RA'.

Skip 'ra' when it appears in a free-text narrative or section header without a preceding oxygen saturation value or clinical context, such as 'on RA' in a non-structured sentence or after a medical procedure.
Skip 'ra' when it appears in a line that is part of a lab or imaging report section, such as 'RA' in 'WBC-12 RA' or 'RBC-4 RA' without a clinical oxygenation context.

Extract 'chest' only when it appears in a clinical context with a body region or imaging modality reference, such as 'CTA of the chest', 'portable chest', or 'chest x-ray', and when followed by a clinical finding or imaging result.

Skip 'chest' when it appears in a free-text narrative within a history of present illness or symptom list without a clinical imaging or diagnostic context, especially when paired with symptoms like 'chest pain' or 'chest discomfort' without an imaging or test result.

Skip 'chest' when it appears in a section header or label such as 'Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure:' or 'History of Present Illness:' unless immediately followed by a clinical imaging or diagnostic finding.

Extract '5' only when it appears as a numerical value in a structured motor strength or reflex assessment line (e.g., 'L  5    ___   ___  5   5    5  5     5     5' or 'R  5    ___   ___  5   5    5  5    5     5'), specifically within sections labeled 'Strength:', 'Neurologic:', or '-Cranial Nerves:' and immediately following a muscle group or reflex name (e.g., 'Delt', 'Bic', 'Tri', 'Pat', 'Ach') with consistent spacing and alignment.

Skip '5' when it appears in a line containing 'Bi Tri Pat Ach' (DTR reflex table header), even if followed by 'L  5' or 'R  5', as these are part of a labeled header row and not actual clinical values.

Skip '5' when it appears in a line with '___' as placeholders (e.g., 'L  5    ___   ___  5   5    5  5     5     5') and no preceding or following clinical values, indicating a template or empty row rather than a documented finding.

Extract 'mild' only when it appears in a clinical assessment line describing a physical exam finding, neurological deficit, or symptom severity, such as 'Mild dysarthria' or 'Mild speech' or 'Mild distress'.

Skip 'mild' when it appears in a diagnostic impression or descriptive phrase within a pathology or endoscopy report, such as 'compatible with mild gastritis' or 'mild candidiasis', even if followed by 'biopsy'.

Skip 'mild' when it appears in a radiology or imaging report context, such as 'mild cardiomegaly' or 'mild stenosis', especially when part of a structured line with a modality or vessel name (e.g., 'mild LAD stenosis').

Extract 'mental status' only when it appears as a labeled heading followed by a clinical assessment (e.g., 'Mental Status: Alert, oriented x 3' or 'Mental Status: Intubated, sedated, unresponsive') within a neurologic or discharge condition section.
Skip 'mental status' when it appears in a narrative sentence without a colon or structured format (e.g., 'His mental status was very altered') even if preceded by a clinical context.
Skip 'mental status' when it appears in a line that is part of a section header or label (e.g., 'Neurologic:', 'Discharge Condition:') and not followed by a colon and clinical assessment.

Extract 'blood' only when it appears in a free-text narrative context describing a clinical condition or finding, such as 'blood. You were started on antibiotics' or 'blood counts were found to be low'.
Skip 'blood' when it appears in a structured lab or test header line that includes '___ [time] BLOOD' followed by a test name (e.g., '___ 06:40AM BLOOD WBC-4.6') or 'BLOOD [test]: [value]'.
Skip 'blood' when it appears as part of a lab test abbreviation or label in a table or line of structured data, such as 'Blood: 11.8' or 'Plt ___' under a 'BLOOD' header.

Extract 'mcv' only when it appears in a structured lab line with numeric values and standard lab notation (e.g., 'MCV-89', 'MCV: 91'), and when preceded by 'RBC', 'Hgb', 'Hct', or similar lab markers in the same line.

Skip 'mcv' when it appears in a free-text narrative line without numeric values or structured lab formatting, such as 'MCV: 91' in a non-lab context or within a section header like 'Reflexes:' or 'Exam notable for:' without lab data.

Skip 'mcv' when it appears in a line containing only '___ [time] BLOOD' followed by lab abbreviations without numeric values or standard lab formatting (e.g., 'MCV: 91' without a number or with '___' placeholder).

Extract 'elevated' only when it appears in a clinical lab or test result context, followed by a lab value or marker (e.g., 'AST/ALT of 139/42, AP 128, Tbili 0.2' or 'troponins were elevated to 0.21').

Skip 'elevated' when it appears in a narrative mental status or mood description without lab context (e.g., 'denies ... elevated or irritable periods' or 'elevated inflammatory markers' without numeric values).
Skip 'elevated' when it appears in a line with '___' as a placeholder and no numeric values or structured lab data (e.g., 'D-dimer was elevated concerning for underlying inflammatory state').

Extract 'iv' only when it appears as part of a medication administration route in a structured medication line, immediately followed by a medication name (e.g., 'IV Dilaudid', 'IV hydralazine'), and within a section labeled with a clinical category such as 'Neurologic', 'CV', or 'In the ED'.

Skip 'iv' when it appears in a narrative sentence that is not part of a medication order or administration instruction, such as 'placed on IV antibiotics' or 'on IV Coumadin', especially when preceded by 'placed on' or 'will continue IV'.
Skip 'iv' when it appears in a line containing '___' as a placeholder and no medication name or structured order format, such as 'You were placed on IV ___' or 'IV ___ while here'.

Extract 'albumin' only when it appears in a structured lab line with a numeric value and lab test delimiter (e.g., 'Albumin-4.1', 'Albumin: 4.3'), and skip when it appears in narrative text without a numeric value or structured lab format (e.g., 'She received albumin').

Skip 'albumin' when it appears in a line containing '___ [time]' followed by a lab test list with no numeric values or lab delimiters (e.g., '___ 12:17AM BLOOD Albumin-4.1' has value, but '___ 04:55PM BLOOD Albumin' without value should be skipped).

Extract 'albumin' only when it appears in a line with a standard lab delimiter such as '-', ':', or '—' followed by a numeric value (e.g., 'Albumin-4.1', 'Albumin: 4.3'), and skip when it appears in a free-text narrative context without such formatting (e.g., 'She received albumin').

Extract 'inr' only when it appears in a structured lab result line with a numeric value immediately following (e.g., 'INR: 3.4', 'INR 3.7'), and not when it appears in discharge instructions or follow-up planning context (e.g., 'INR checked on ___', 'INR should be drawn as per ___ clinic').

Skip 'inr' when it appears in a sentence that includes 'follow up', 'draw', 'checked', or 'recommended' in the context of scheduling or patient instructions (e.g., 'INR checked on ___', 'recommending a draw on ___'), even if followed by a numeric value.

Extract 'inr' only when it is part of a lab result line that includes standard lab delimiters such as '-', ':', or '—' and is followed by a numeric value (e.g., 'INR-3.4', 'INR: 1.4'), and skip when it appears in free-text narrative without such formatting or numeric context.

Extract 'face' only when it appears in a clinical neurological or physical exam context, specifically within cranial nerve assessments (e.g., 'VII: Face is symmetric...') or in descriptions of focal neurological deficits (e.g., 'numbness in the face', 'weakness in the face') with clinical symptomatology.

Skip 'face' when it appears in a free-text physical exam line that lists body regions without clinical descriptors, such as 'moving all 4 extremities with purpose, face symmetric' — only extract if paired with abnormal findings or neurological assessment.

Skip 'face' when it appears in a line containing '___' as a placeholder and no associated clinical findings or structured exam notation (e.g., 'face ___' or 'face symmetric' without preceding symptom or exam detail).

Extract 'bp' only when it appears in a vitals or physical exam line with a numeric blood pressure value in format 'X/Y' (e.g., 'BP: 134/84'), and preceded by 'T:', 'P:', 'R:', or 'SaO2:' or similar vital signs markers.
Skip 'bp' when it appears in a line that contains '___' as a placeholder, or in a narrative line discussing BP management without a numeric value (e.g., 'allow BP to autoregulate', 'BP controlled').

Skip 'bp' when it appears in a section header or bullet point that is not part of a structured vitals or physical exam line, such as '# Neuro:', '#HYPERTENSION', or in a line with only 'BP' and no following numeric value or vital sign context.

Extract 'cxr' only when it appears as part of a clinical imaging finding or report line that includes a description of radiographic findings (e.g., 'CXR demonstrated', 'CXR revealed', 'CXR was without', 'CXR showed'), and is not preceded by a section placeholder like '___'.

Skip 'cxr' when it appears in a line containing '___' as a placeholder immediately before or after the term, especially when the line is part of a section header or template structure (e.g., 'CXR ___:', '___ CXR:')
Skip 'cxr' when it appears in a line that is part of a structured section header or bullet point list without a clinical finding or imaging result description (e.g., '- CXR', 'CXR ___:')

Extract 'gait' only when it appears in a structured neurologic or physical exam line with a clinical descriptor (e.g., 'Good initiation', 'Narrow-based', 'not tested', 'deferred') and is preceded by a section header like '-DTRs:', 'Neurologic:', or 'Reflexes:'.

Skip 'gait' when it appears in a free-text narrative line that includes 'training', 'therapy', 'home therapy', or 'falls prevention' without clinical exam descriptors, especially in sections like 'Brief Hospital Course' or 'History of Present Illness'.
Skip 'gait' when it appears in a line containing 'denied difficulty with' or 'felt continued' and is not followed by a clinical exam descriptor or structured exam format.

Extract 'pelvic' only when it appears as a section header followed by a clinical finding or imaging result, specifically when preceded by a line with 'Pelvic:' or 'PELVIS:' and followed by a clinical descriptor such as 'no free fluid', 'no adenopathy', or 'performed in ED'.

Skip 'pelvic' when it appears in a line that is part of a structured anatomical listing (e.g., 'No pelvic side-wall or inguinal lymphadenopathy') without a clinical descriptor or imaging result, especially when the line is a continuation of a bulleted list with no new clinical information.

Extract 'pelvic' when it is part of a phrase indicating a clinical exam or imaging modality, such as 'pelvic U/S' or 'pelvic exam', especially when followed by a finding or result; skip when it appears in a generic anatomical list without clinical context.

Extract 'evaluation' only when it appears in a clinical context preceded by a clinical action or condition (e.g., 'neurologic evaluation', 'further outpatient EP evaluation', 'evaluation of bradycardia'), and followed by a clinical finding or plan.

Skip 'evaluation' when it appears in a narrative line that includes 'prior to discharge' or 'follow-up' without a clinical action or plan, especially when paired with 'Physical Therapy' or 'PCP' as in 'PT for evaluation prior to discharge'.
Skip 'evaluation' when it appears in a line containing '___' as a placeholder, or in a free-text line without a clinical descriptor or structured follow-up plan.

Extract 'diet' only when it appears in a line that is part of a structured instruction or clinical plan, specifically when followed by a dietary stage (e.g., 'Stage III diet', 'clear liquid diet', 'soft diet') or a directive to 'advance' or 'resume' diet.

Skip 'diet' when it appears in a narrative line that describes patient status or functional ability (e.g., 'tolerating a stage 3 diet', 'ambulating, voiding without assistance') without a clinical instruction or dietary stage specification.
Extract 'diet' when it appears in a line immediately followed by a clinical directive such as 'do not self advance', 'stay on', or 'resume', especially in discharge instructions or care plans.

Extract 'arteries' only when it appears in a clinical imaging or anatomical description context with anatomical descriptors such as 'anterior and posterior circulation', 'supplying blood to your heart', or 'of the head', and is followed by a clinical finding (e.g., 'no stenosis', 'obstruction', 'normal flow signal').

Skip 'arteries' when it appears in a line containing '___' as a placeholder or in a fragmented anatomical listing (e.g., 'the celiac, SMA and right and left renal arteries originate from the true lumen'), especially when the term is part of a list without a clinical assessment.

Skip 'arteries' when it appears in a line that is part of a structured section header or bullet point list (e.g., 'CONTRAINDICATIONS FOR IV CONTRAST') and is not followed by a clinical finding or imaging result.

Extract 'plt' only when it appears as part of a structured hematology lab line with a numeric value immediately following (e.g., 'Plt-123*'), and preceded by a valid lab header line containing 'BLOOD' and a timestamp.
Skip 'plt' when it appears in a line that contains '___' as a placeholder and is not immediately followed by a numeric lab value or lab modifier (e.g., 'Plt ___' with no value or symbol).

Skip 'plt' when it appears in a line that is part of a fragmented or incomplete lab listing where no lab value or modifier follows, and the line is not preceded by a valid lab header (e.g., 'MCV-89 MCH-30.2 MCHC-34.1 RDW-16.3* Plt ___').

Extract 'aspirin' only when followed by a dose (e.g., 'aspirin 81mg', 'aspirin 325mg') or a medication regimen including a dose (e.g., 'aspirin and atorvastatin', 'aspirin + Plavix'). Skip when 'aspirin' appears in a bullet point list without a dose or in a general instruction context (e.g., 'continue to take aspirin') without dosing.

Skip 'aspirin' when it appears in a line that is part of a structured instruction or discharge plan that uses 'continue' or 'will continue' without specifying a dose or regimen (e.g., 'continue to take aspirin', 'will continue on aspirin').

Extract 'aspirin' only when it appears in a clinical context with a specific medication action (e.g., 'started on aspirin', 'placed on aspirin', 'will require aspirin') and is associated with a clinical decision or diagnosis (e.g., stroke, cardiac cath, stents). Skip when 'aspirin' appears in a generic instruction or follow-up line without clinical context.

Extract 'stenosis' only when it appears in a clinical imaging or vascular assessment context, specifically when followed by anatomical descriptors (e.g., 'P1 segment', 'carotid artery', 'vertebral artery') or in proximity to vascular findings like 'occlusion', 'aneurysm', or 'normal flow signal'.

Skip 'stenosis' when it appears in a line containing '___' as a placeholder or in a fragmented sentence without anatomical or imaging context (e.g., '___ stenosis' or 'diffuse mild stenosis') unless immediately followed by a specific vessel name.

Skip 'stenosis' when it appears in a line that is part of a structured section header, bullet list, or free-text narrative without clinical imaging or vascular description (e.g., '___ stenosis' in a placeholder line or 'stenosis' in a discharge plan without anatomical context).

Extract 'imaging' only when it appears as part of a clinical sentence that describes diagnostic test results or findings, specifically when followed by a clinical outcome or anatomical description (e.g., 'imaging showed a new infarct', 'imaging of your abdomen demonstrated').

Skip 'imaging' when it appears in a section header or structured label line that is part of a placeholder or formatting pattern, such as 'IMAGING: ======' or '___ Imaging CHEST', even if followed by a clinical phrase.

Skip 'imaging' when it appears in a line that is part of a fragmented or incomplete listing with no clinical context, such as lines with only 'IMAGING:' followed by a blank or non-clinical label (e.g., 'IMAGING: _________').

Extract 'dilated' only when it appears in a clinical imaging or anatomical description context with a body part or structure immediately preceding it (e.g., 'aortic valve leaflets appear structurally normal with good leaflet excursion and mildly dilated', 'left atrium is mildly dilated').

Skip 'dilated' when it appears in a line that is part of a fragmented or incomplete sentence without a clear anatomical or clinical structure (e.g., 'dilated. No atrial septal defect is seen by 2D or color Doppler') unless followed by a body part or structure.
Skip 'dilated' when it appears in a line that contains '___' as a placeholder or in a structured section header (e.g., 'TTE (___):' context) even if it is followed by a body part.
Extract 'ldh' only when it appears in a structured lab line with a numeric value immediately following, formatted as 'LD(LDH)-[number]*' or 'LD(LDH)-[number]' (e.g., 'LD(LDH)-491*').

Skip 'ldh' when it appears in a narrative sentence that describes a lab value in relation to baseline or prior status, such as 'slightly elevated LDH (her baseline)' or 'LDH elevated in context of prior illness'.
Skip 'ldh' when it appears in a line that contains '___' as a placeholder and is not part of a complete lab value line with a numeric result.

Extract 'pcp' only when it appears in a clinical context with a follow-up instruction or plan, specifically when followed by 'follow up with your PCP', 'follow up with PCP', or 'PCP ___' (with placeholder), and is within a section labeled 'Discharge Instructions', 'History of Present Illness', 'Hospital Course', or 'Brief Hospital Course'.

Skip 'pcp' when it appears in a line that contains '___' as a placeholder and is part of a fragmented or incomplete sentence without a clinical follow-up plan, especially when the line is part of a medication or symptom list with no explicit follow-up directive.

Extract 'pcp' only when it appears in a sentence that includes a clinical action such as 'will be followed with', 'should follow up with', or 'to have further workup of', and is not part of a structured medication list or bullet point with no clinical context.

Extract 'palpable' only when it appears in a clinical physical exam context with a body part or lesion description, specifically when followed by an anatomical descriptor (e.g., 'nodule in LLQ', 'deformity', 'pulses') or a clinical finding (e.g., 'non-tender', 'mobile') within the same sentence or line.

Skip 'palpable' when it appears in a standalone line or as part of a structured section header, bullet list, or formatted table entry (e.g., 'Palpable (x)' in a vascular pulse assessment line), unless directly followed by a clinical descriptor of a physical finding.
Skip 'palpable' when it appears in a line that contains '___' as a placeholder or in a fragmented sentence without a clear clinical descriptor of a physical exam finding (e.g., 'palpable. No edema.')

Extract 'follow-up' when it appears in a clinical context within a sentence that describes a planned future clinical visit or test, especially when followed by a specialty (e.g., 'follow-up with neurology', 'follow-up with orthopedics'), or when part of a structured plan line such as 'follow-up in ___ weeks' or 'follow-up scheduled with ___'.

Skip 'follow-up' when it appears in a standalone line or as part of a placeholder section header such as 'Followup Instructions:' or '___', or when it is embedded in a fragmented or incomplete sentence with '___' as a placeholder, even if the surrounding text suggests a future visit.

Skip 'follow-up' when it appears in a narrative sentence that is purely patient education or discharge instruction (e.g., 'you should see your doctor in ___ few weeks') and is not tied to a specific clinical plan or specialty referral, especially if preceded by 'We recommend that you see...' or 'You will have follow-up in outpatient ___ clinic'.
Extract 'vs' only when it appears as a structured header followed immediately by numeric vital signs (e.g., 'VS: 98.7 118/66 66 16 99RA') in a clinical exam or admission section.
Skip 'vs' when it appears in a line containing '___' as a placeholder or in a fragmented sentence without complete vital sign values (e.g., 'VS: ___ 1655 Temp: 98.1')

Skip 'vs' when it appears in a narrative sentence that describes a past event without current or documented values (e.g., 'initial VS were 98.1 140 132/67') unless followed by a complete numeric vital sign set.

Extract 'follow up' only when it appears in a clinical follow-up instruction with a specific provider name or time frame (e.g., 'follow up with Dr. ___ in 2 weeks' or 'follow up with ___ as scheduled').
Skip 'follow up' when it appears in a line containing '___' as a placeholder or in a fragmented sentence without a clear clinical plan (e.g., 'follow up with ___ for further follow up').
Skip 'follow up' when it appears in a standalone line or as part of a section header such as 'Followup Instructions' or 'Followup in ___'.

Extract 'eyes' only when it appears as a structured header in a physical exam or clinical section, followed by a clinical description of ocular findings (e.g., 'EYES: Anicteric, pupils equally round' or 'Left eye opens, right does not').
